title: Brain Computer Interfaces
answer: Brain computer interfaces are systems that read neural signals and translate them into commands for external devices, or stimulate the brain in response to computed intent. In neuroinformatics they sit between clinical neurophysiology, signal processing, and assistive technology. The site's medical AI model tracking includes models used for decoding motor imagery, speech attempts, and seizure patterns, though BCI-specific models are a subset of the 1000 medical AI models. crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Brain computer interfaces are systems that read neural signals and translate them into commands for external devices, or stimulate the brain in response to computed intent. In neuroinformatics they sit between clinical neurophysiology, signal processing, and assistive technology. The site's medical AI model tracking includes models used for decoding motor imagery, speech attempts, and seizure patterns, though BCI-specific models are a subset of the 1000 medical AI models. Scope covers invasive and non-invasive recording, real-time decoding, and closed-loop stimulation for movement, communication, and monitoring.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: BCIs depend on sensor arrays, amplifiers, and edge or bedside compute. Non-invasive systems use electroencephalography caps, while invasive systems use implanted microelectrode arrays or electrocorticography grids. Data flows from the sensor to a processing unit that runs feature extraction and decoding models, often on a local machine to keep latency low. Some research systems stream to hospital servers or cloud for offline analysis, but clinical use favors on-device inference.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Neural signals are filtered, artifact-corrected, and converted into features such as band power, spike rates, or time-frequency maps. A decoder, often a linear classifier, Kalman filter, or recurrent network, maps those features to intended actions or words. Training uses calibration sessions where the person imagines movement or attempts speech while the system records paired labels. Closed-loop systems then update the decoder as neural patterns drift.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: BCI data is intimate and can reveal mood, fatigue, or intent, so consent, data minimization, and deletion rights matter. Product liability questions arise when implanted hardware or decoding software fails, and the site tracks six active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, though not all involve BCI. Regulatory pages cover device classification, clinical trial oversight, and data protection. Provenance includes the recording hardware, calibration session, model version, and any clinician-approved mapping.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The field is moving toward higher-bandwidth, lower-power implants and better non-invasive decoding of continuous speech and handwriting. Research is exploring adaptive decoders that recalibrate without long sessions and closed-loop stimulation for mood, memory, and movement disorders. As models become part of regulated medical devices, the site's compliance and regulation pages will need to track BCI-specific guidance alongside general AI medical device rules. The practical goal is reliable, safe communication and control for people with severe motor impairment, not consumer enhancement.
